robot: two 6-joint ALOHA (ViperX) arms with parallel-jaw grippers on a fixed base

frame.suite: the service's world frame: origin at the robot's kinematic root link on its mounting, +z up
frame.base_text: the robot base frame: origin at the robot's root link (the origin of the service's frame), +Z up; +X is the service frame's +y axis (across the table, between the two arms) and +Y its -x axis (towards the left arm)

left.note: 6 joints (waist, shoulder, elbow, forearm_roll, wrist_angle, wrist_rotate; rad). Tool frame (TCP): a point near the closed finger pads, approach axis (hand to fingertips) = its local +x, fingers close along its local y; the fingertips reach about 16 mm beyond it.

ee.point: the gripper's tool frame (TCP), near the closed finger pads
ee.mode_text: the service solves each pose by inverse kinematics (no collision checking) and drives the arm there in joint space; move_robot sends the path as poses about 1.5 cm apart

right.note: 6 joints (waist, shoulder, elbow, forearm_roll, wrist_angle, wrist_rotate; rad). Tool frame (TCP): a point near the closed finger pads, approach axis (hand to fingertips) = its local +x, fingers close along its local y; the fingertips reach about 16 mm beyond it.

ee.point: the gripper's tool frame (TCP), near the closed finger pads
ee.mode_text: the service solves each pose by inverse kinematics (no collision checking) and drives the arm there in joint space; move_robot sends the path as poses about 1.5 cm apart

notes: The episode ends by itself at the first success (all of the task's final conditions holding for its confirmation time: after the last move let simulated time pass with wait or observe seconds), when the task's own failure predicate fires (reason task_failed) or when your time is up; there is no step budget and nothing to signal. End-effector goals are solved by the service's inverse kinematics (no collision checking) and driven to in joint space; a solution more than 0.5 rad from the current joints on any joint is refused for that arm (it holds), so long end-effector moves go in steps of a few cm and degrees. Arm joint targets move at most 0.04 rad per control step; a faster request takes the steps it needs. No gripper target goes lower than 15 mm below the tabletop. Grasping is assisted (spec robot_spec.grippers states the rule): closing on a graspable part inside its grasp region takes hold of it, and any command that opens the gripper by more than 0.2 % of its travel lets it go. The gripper value in the state is the command in force; gripper_opening_m is the measured gap between the finger pads. Joint efforts (proprio_now, *_effort) rise when an arm pushes on something.

patch.robot: a 7-joint Franka Panda arm with a Robotiq 2F-85 parallel gripper on a fixed base

frame.base_text: the robot base frame: the arm's root link (the origin of the service's frame), +X forward from the arm base, +Y left, +Z up

arm.note: 7 joints (joint1..joint7; rad). Tool frame (TCP): a point near the closed finger pads, approach axis (hand to fingertips) = its local +z, fingers close along its local y; the fingertips reach about 6 mm beyond it.

ee.point: the gripper's tool frame (TCP), near the closed finger pads
ee.mode_text: the service solves each pose by inverse kinematics (no collision checking) and drives the arm there in joint space; move_robot sends the path as poses about 1.5 cm apart

patch.robot: two 7-joint Franka Panda arms, each with a two-finger Panda hand (tendon-coupled fingers)

frame.suite: the service's world frame: origin at the left arm's base link on its mounting, +z up, x along that arm's forward direction
frame.base_text: the robot base frame: the left arm's base link (the origin of the service's frame), +X that arm's forward direction, +Z up; the right arm's base pose in it is spec robot_spec.base.right

left.note: 7 joints (actuator1..actuator7; rad; joint 7, the wrist, has no joint limit). The end-effector pose is the tool-frame site between the fingertips. Gripper command 0 = closed (the hand squeezes at its tendon force limit, about 70 N per finger) .. 255 = open.

right.note: 7 joints (actuator1..actuator7; rad; joint 7, the wrist, has no joint limit). The end-effector pose is the tool-frame site between the fingertips. Gripper command 0 = closed (the hand squeezes at its tendon force limit, about 70 N per finger) .. 255 = open.

patch.notes: The arms take joint targets only: an end-effector goal is solved with the service's inverse kinematics (damped least squares on the robot model, no collision checking, within 1 mm and 0.01 rad) and sent as joint rows. Control runs at 400 Hz (2.5 ms per control step). Arm joint targets move at most at the arm's joint speed limits (spec robot_spec.controller); a faster request takes the control steps it needs. The gripper command switches at the row. Grasps are physical: friction from the finger contacts, nothing attaches a part to a gripper. The episode ends by itself at the first settled success (the task's requirements hold, no robot link touches any part and every part is at rest, then again after the last row is held 1 s more), on a simulator breakdown (reason sim_breakdown) or when your time is up; there is no step budget and nothing to signal. The gripper value in the state is the command in force; gripper_opening_m is the measured opening. Actuator forces (proprio_now, *_effort) rise when an arm pushes on something.

left.note: 6 joints (waist, shoulder, elbow, forearm_roll, wrist_angle, wrist_rotate; rad; wrist_rotate has no joint limit). The end-effector pose is the tool-frame site between the fingertips. Gripper command: finger rail position, 0.002 m = closed .. 0.037 m = open.

right.note: 6 joints (waist, shoulder, elbow, forearm_roll, wrist_angle, wrist_rotate; rad; wrist_rotate has no joint limit). The end-effector pose is the tool-frame site between the fingertips. Gripper command: finger rail position, 0.002 m = closed .. 0.037 m = open.
